Julia Faye: Julia Faye (born September 24, 1893 – April 6, 1966) was an American actress who appeared in over 200 films during the silent and early sound era. She began her career as a child actress in 1913, and worked extensively as an extra before landing her breakthrough role in the 1917 film "A Romance of the Redwoods". Faye became a fixture at Warner Bros. Studios in the 1920s, appearing in films such as "The Jazz Singer" (1927) and "The Maltese Falcon" (1931). She was also known for her work in several Cecil B. DeMille productions, including "The Ten Commandments" (1923) and "The King of Kings" (1927). Faye's career declined in the 1930s, and she retired from acting in 1943. She died in 1966 at the age of 72.
Carlos Santana: Carlos Santana is a Mexican and American guitarist and songwriter born on July 20, 1947, in Autlán de Navarro, Mexico. He moved to San Francisco in the early 1960s where he formed the band Santana, which became popular for their fusion of rock, blues, and Latin American music. Santana is known for his distinctive guitar style, which incorporates elements of blues, jazz, and world music. He has won 10 Grammy Awards and three Latin Grammy Awards and has sold more than 100 million records worldwide. Some of his most famous songs include "Oye Como Va," "Black Magic Woman," and "Smooth." Santana was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1998. He is also known for his philanthropic work, including the establishment of the Milagro Foundation, which supports education, health, and the arts for underprivileged children.
Marianne McAndrew: Marianne McAndrew is an American actress and singer, born on November 21, 1942, in Cleveland, Ohio. She began her acting career in the late 1960s, appearing in various television shows and films. Her notable film appearances include the role of Irene Molloy in the 1969 film adaptation of the musical "Hello, Dolly!", and as Princess Zareta in the 1976 film "The Blue Bird". She also had recurring roles on popular television shows such as "The Love Boat" and "Fantasy Island". In addition to her acting career, McAndrew was a trained singer and performed in various stage productions, including the Broadway production of "The King and I". She retired from acting in the 1990s and currently resides in California.
Eiffel Tower: The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower in Paris, France. It was designed and built by Gustave Eiffel's company and completed in 1899. The tower is 330 metres tall. It was the tallest man-made structure in the world until the Chrysler Building in New York City was finished in 1930.
